newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed,sterling to fall further.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed,sterling to fall further.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mixed, as yen, marks and Swiss francs held strong gains, while sterling and Canadian dollars remained lower and appear poised for more declines, some floor traders and analysts said.
"A lot of the action in the dollar has been because of the unwinding of sterling/mark positions," an analyst said.
One technical analyst said September sterling futures are in a long-term downtrend, adding that $1.5650 is the contract's next support level on a weekly continuation chart.
"Sterling really went into a downtrend when it took out $1.6616 on July 25," he said.
He said this week's price action, which culminated on Friday with a break of the contract low settlement of $1.5792, deepened some traders' convictions for larger sterling losses.
September sterling remained below the pivot point at $1.5892 during Friday's session, falling through the five-month settlement low of $1.5858 in early trade.

Another analyst said technicals for Canadian dollars were shaky after September fell through support at $0.7200. A close below $0.7196 in the near term would signal a less neutral position for Canadian dollars which have been in sideways range since late spring.
Meanwhile, September marks could rally to $0.5728, which is equivalent to 1.75 spot marks, and still hold its bearish trend, analysts said.

One currency trader said September marks are more likely to close above $0.5492 before re-testing its contract low of $0.5303, which corresponded to the dollar/mark's 7-3/4-year high of 1.8910 spot this week.

On the other hand, Swiss franc and yen futures were on the cusp of firming their technicals. September yen needed to close above $0.008775 to turn its trend higher. The contract closed up $0.000280 at $0.008766.
"How bullish the yen would get, I don't know, but you would have turned the trend around," a technical analyst said.

September yen rose $0.000324 to $0.008810, a three-and-a-half month high, on heavy dollar selling by funds. One analyst also said Japanese firms and exporters liquidated U.S. assets to lighten their dollar inventory ahead of Japan's Obon holidays in mid-August.
He said the dollar selling may have also been based on concerns about the U.S.'s current account figures.
Some traders were looking for September to test its initial daily price limit of $0.000400.

However, buying in both the yen and Swiss franc pit slowed down in the afternoon, as the dollar's downside correction was overshadowed by the robust sell-offs in both the U.S. T-bond and U.S. stock markets, traders said.
September Swiss francs needed to close above $0.6670 to "potentially turn things bullish," one trader saidd.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was up $0.000280 at $0.008766, marks were up $0.0059 at $0.5426, Swiss francs were $0.0088 higher at $0.6650, sterling were off $0.0018 at $1.5840, Canadian dollars were off $0.0011 at $0.7209, Australian dollars were up $0.0049 at $0.7351 and Mexican pesos were $0.000075 higher at $0.126150. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
